description: Native PE beacon agent for the AdaptixC2 open-source red-team framework. Compiled with MinGW/GCC. Uses RC4-encrypted config in .rdata, modified DJB2 hashing for API resolution, and WinINet-based HTTP/S C2 communication.
Go-based agent for the AdaptixC2 framework. Uses AES-128-GCM encrypted config with msgpack serialization.
.NET info-stealer/keylogger. Config stored as static string fields in a settings class, encrypted with AES-256-CBC (or XOR in older variants). Exfiltrates via SMTP, FTP, Telegram, or HTTP POST.

Open-source .NET RAT. Config stored in encrypted static fields in Settings class. Uses AES-256-CBC with PBKDF2-derived key (50,000 iterations). Supports keylogging, screen capture, file management, and plugin loading.

Commercial adversary simulation tool. Agent (Badger) uses RC4-encrypted config (Base64-wrapped pre-v1.3), direct/indirect syscalls for API calls, and supports HTTP/S, DNS over HTTPS (DoH), and SMB transports. Designed for EDR evasion.

Commercial adversary simulation beacon. Uses ROR13 hash-based API resolution in shellcode stagers, XOR-encrypted TLV config in .data section, and RSA+AES encrypted C2 communications. Highly configurable via Malleable C2 profiles.
.NET C2 framework. Grunt implant uses AES-256-CBC + RSA-2048 hybrid encryption. JSON-formatted messages with GUID-based task tracking. Supports HTTP, SMB, and bridge listeners.

Legacy RAT with GUI builder. Config stored in PE resource named 'DCDATA' (or numbered resource), RC4-encrypted with a key derived from version string. Identified by '#KCMDDC' command prefix and distinctive string patterns.
Delphi-compiled loader/RAT sold as MaaS. Uses custom Base64 alphabet for config encoding. Often delivered via AutoIt scripts (AU3!EA06 magic). Config contains C2 URLs, flags, and campaign settings.
Open-source Go-based C2 framework. Uses RSA/AES-256 hybrid encryption. Supports HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, DoH, and QUIC transports. Go binary with embedded RSA public key and C2 configuration.

Modular banking trojan turned malware distribution platform. C2 list stored as XOR-encrypted (IP, port) pairs in .data section. Uses ECDH key exchange, AES-encrypted protobuf C2 protocol, and Zlib-compressed payloads.

Chinese-origin RAT with leaked source code, leading to many variants. Identified by 5-byte magic header ('Gh0st' or variant) in network traffic, Zlib-compressed packets, and 13-byte packet header structure.

Open-source C2 framework agent. Uses DJB2 hashing (seed 5381, toupper) for API resolution via PEB walking, AES-256-CTR for C2 traffic encryption, and RC4 (SystemFunction032) for sleep obfuscation. Compiled with MinGW cross-compiler.
ua: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1; WOW64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/96.0.4664.110 Safari/537.36

description: Banking trojan and malware loader. Initial loader contacts hardcoded C2 to retrieve encrypted payload. Uses RC4 encryption, steganographic config in PNG images, and mimics Google Analytics cookie format in C2 beaconing.

C/C++ info-stealer sold as MaaS. Uses MurmurHash2 (seed 0x20) for string hashing and ChaCha20 for config encryption. Steals browser data, crypto wallets, and credentials. Frequent updates with evolving obfuscation.

Go-based C2 framework supporting HTTP/2, HTTP/3 (QUIC), and h2c transports. Uses JWE (PBES2_HS512_A256KW) for message encryption and OPAQUE PAKE for authentication. Go binary with distinctive protocol negotiation.

Metasploit Framework's advanced payload. Uses ROR13 API hashing in stagers (identical algorithm to Cobalt Strike). Differentiated by URI checksum algorithm (checksum8 values), TLV command protocol, and AES-256 transport encryption.
.NET agent for the Mythic C2 framework. Uses AES-256 PSK for initial comms and RSA-4096 EKE (Encrypted Key Exchange) for session key negotiation. JSON-based message format with UUID-based tasking.

.NET RAT with plugin architecture. Config encrypted with DES-CBC, key derived from a GUID string via PBKDF2. Supports plugin-based extensibility with modules for keylogging, surveillance, and credential theft.
Commercial C2 implant by MDSec. Identified by custom PE sections (.profile, .detourc, .detourd) and YARA-verified hex patterns. Uses advanced evasion techniques including syscall proxying.

.NET RAT widely used since 2013. Config stored as plaintext or lightly obfuscated static fields. Uses a distinctive pipe separator '|'|'|' in C2 communications. Supports keylogging, webcam, file management, remote shell.

Modular loader with anti-analysis capabilities. Uses dual-layer encryption: RC4 for outer layer, AES-CBC for inner config data. Heavy anti-debugging and anti-VM checks. Multi-component: loader + core module.

Modular RAT associated with Chinese APT groups. Config encrypted with XOR+RC4+LZNT1 compression. Identified by 'PLUG' magic (0x504C5547) in decrypted config header. ShadowPad is a related/successor platform.
Legacy RAT widely used by APT groups. Uses Camellia-256-ECB encryption with password-derived key. Default password is 'admin', default port 3460. Config and C2 comms use the same Camellia cipher.

Open-source C2 framework with PowerShell and C# implants. Uses AES-256 encryption for C2 communications. Identified by specific PowerShell patterns, hardcoded key material, and YARA-verified indicators.

Banking trojan and malware loader active since 2008. Config stored in PE resources (IDs 3/311 or 118/524), RC4-encrypted with SHA1/SHA256-derived keys. Campaign IDs (bb, obama, azd) track distribution campaigns.

Open-source .NET RAT. Similar architecture to AsyncRAT — Settings class with AES-encrypted fields and PBKDF2 key derivation. Supports remote desktop, keylogging, file management, reverse proxy, and registry editor.

C/C++ info-stealer (v2 rewrite of original Raccoon). Uses RC4+Base64 for config/comms encryption. Identified by 'Record' User-Agent and specific mutex value. Steals browser data, wallets, and application credentials.

.NET info-stealer sold as MaaS. Config contains C2 IP:port and BuildID. Uses Base64+XOR encoding for config strings. Communicates via .NET Remoting (net.tcp:// WCF protocol) with SOAP-serialized messages.

Commercial RAT (marketed as 'Remote Control & Surveillance'). Config stored as RC4-encrypted blob in PE resource named 'SETTINGS' (or 'RCData'). Key is first N bytes of the resource. Fields separated by 0x7C1F1E1E7C delimiter.

Open-source Go-based C2 framework by BishopFox. Supports mTLS, WireGuard, HTTP/S, and DNS transports. Implants are compiled Go binaries with embedded protobuf-serialized configs. No hash-based API resolution.

C/C++ info-stealer based on Vidar/Raccoon codebases. Uses RC4+Base64 encoding for C2 communications. Anti-sandbox checks look for 'HAL9TH' computer name and 'JohnDoe' username. Steals browser data and wallets.

C++ info-stealer, fork of Arkei. Uses dead-drop resolvers (social media profiles) for C2 URL retrieval. Downloads DLL dependencies at runtime. Config received from C2 as plaintext after initial beacon.

.NET RAT with modular plugin architecture. Config stored as AES-256-ECB encrypted static fields in a Settings class, keyed by MD5 hash of the Mutex field. Uses raw TCP with a configurable separator (default '<Xwormmm>') and supports USB spreading, keylogging, HVNC, and DDoS.

Native C++ RAT with RC4-encrypted config in the .bss PE section. Uses raw TCP for C2 with RC4 encryption (key 'warzone160\x00'). Features include remote VNC, reverse shell, process hollowing, browser/email credential harvesting, keylogging, and UAC bypass via IFileOperation.

.NET RAT with modular plugin architecture and its own IDE (DCRat Studio). Config is Base64-encoded, zlib-compressed, and AES-256-CBC encrypted with PBKDF-derived key and HMAC verification. Uses hash-based command dispatch to avoid plaintext command strings.

.NET RAT forked from AsyncRAT with additional HVNC, Clipper, and Telegram control modules. Config uses identical AES-256-CBC encryption scheme as AsyncRAT. Features certificate-pinned TLS for C2 and can dynamically retrieve C2 addresses from Pastebin.

Modified Gh0st RAT variant used by SneakyChef APT. Key differentiator is an 8-byte packet header (versus 5-byte in classic Gh0st RAT). Delivered via multi-stage chain using DLL sideloading, XOR decryption, and aPLib decompression. Features ODBC registry reconnaissance.

Open-source .NET RAT with HVNC, SOCKS5 reverse proxy, live microphone capture, and multiple UAC bypass methods. Config includes IP, port, mutex, encryption password, and authentication string. MoonPeak is a North Korean (UAT-5394/Kimsuky) modified variant with tight client-server version coupling.

Legitimate remote administration tool frequently abused by threat actors. Config stored in plaintext client32.ini file. C2 communication via HTTP POST with distinctive 'fakeurl.htm' gateway URL and 'NetSupport Manager/1.3' User-Agent. Drop package includes characteristic set of DLLs.

.NET RAT with hidden secondary desktop capability for browser manipulation. Uses AES-256 encryption for C2 with a 32-byte key stored as 'rawData' variable. Protected by 'calli' obfuscator (ModC) that replaces normal method calls with calli IL instructions. Communicates over TCP on atypical ports (15647, 15678, 15649, 15847).

C-based ransomware with code lineage from BlackMatter/DarkSide. Requires a -pass command-line argument to decrypt the main payload routine (environment keying). Uses XOR key 0x4506DFCA for string decryption and a BlackMatter-derived API hashing algorithm with NOT+XOR finalization (constant 0x29009fe6). Supports AES-256, ChaCha20, or RSA-2048 encryption with intermittent encryption mode.

First major Rust-based ransomware (November 2021). Cross-platform (Windows PE, Linux ELF, ESXi). Requires mandatory --access-token argument for config decryption and execution gating. JSON configuration embedded in binary with configurable AES or ChaCha20 encryption. Sphynx (v2) was a complete rewrite with enhanced evasion.

C++ ransomware using Boost ASIO for multithreading, spdlog for logging, ADVobfuscator for string obfuscation, and Nettle for crypto. Megazord variant (Aug 2023) and Akira_v2 (April 2024) are Rust rewrites. Uses ChaCha20 for file encryption with RSA key wrapping. Early versions had a PRNG vulnerability (nanosecond timestamp seed) enabling decryption.

C++ ransomware using ChaCha20 for file encryption with RSA-4096 key wrapping. Uses ADVobfuscator for stack-based string obfuscation with single-byte XOR. Deploys SystemBC as Tor proxy for C2 tunneling. Known mutex 'dsajdhas.0' and wallpaper file 'dlaksjdoiwq.jpg'.

C++ ransomware using AES (via OpenSSL) for file encryption with RSA key wrapping. Rebranded to BlackSuit in 2024. Uses intermittent encryption based on file size. Requires mandatory -name argument (32-character victim ID). Known mutex 'Global\WLm87eV1oNRx6P3E4Cy9'. Linux variant compiled with GCC.

C++ ransomware recompiled per campaign (unique hashes per deployment). Uses AES-256 + RSA hybrid encryption with intermittent encryption pattern (alternating 0x100000-byte encrypted/skipped chunks). Appends .PLAY extension. Associated with PlusBrute custom brute-force tool.

Ransomware compiled with MinGW GNU 6.3.0 using LibTomCrypt library. Uses ChaCha20 with 256-bit key for file encryption and RSA-4096 for key wrapping. Had a PRNG vulnerability (execution time nanoseconds as seed) enabling decryption until patched. Multi-threaded with thread count equal to CPU processor count.

C++ ransomware (distinct from MedusaLocker). Uses AES-256 for file encryption with RSA-2048/4096 key management. String decryption via XOR with single-byte key 0x2E. Terminates 280+ Windows services and processes. Known mutex '8761ABBD-7F85-42EE-B272-A76179687C63'. Primary encryptor binary named 'gaze.exe'.

Go-based ransomware (Windows/Linux) with C++ ESXi variant. Code overlap with BlackCat/Knight. Uses Curve25519 ECDH + AES hybrid encryption with intermittent encryption (0x100000-byte chunks skipping 0x200000 bytes). Requires mandatory -pass argument (32-byte passphrase) for config decryption. File extension derived from first 6 chars of Curve25519 public key.

C++ ransomware associated with supply-chain exploitation campaigns (MOVEit, Cleo MFT). Uses AES with per-file random key encrypted by embedded RSA-1024 public key. Notable for variable mutex names (e.g., 'MoneyP#666', 'Clop^_-', 'Fany-Fany-6-6-6') and burst operational pattern (dormant periods followed by mass exploitation).

Ransomware using AES-256 for file encryption with RSA-2048 key wrapping. Creates debug log file 'DbgLog.sys' in %AppData% with runtime status. Requires mandatory -id argument (6-character value) for execution. Known for extremely fast attack timelines (initial access to full encryption in under 2 hours). Primarily targets education sector via compromised VPN credentials.

C++ ransomware using AES-128-CTR for file encryption with Curve25519 (Donna implementation) for key exchange and SHA512 for key derivation. Supports fast/medium/slow encryption modes. Multi-threaded with thread count equal to CPU cores * 4. Source code sold for ~$300K in March 2024. Lynx ransomware is a derivative with 70%+ code overlap.

C++ infostealer with multi-stage shellcode architecture and custom virtual machine (Q3VM) for code virtualization. Loader config encrypted with RC4, main module uses AES derived from ECDH (NIST P-256) shared secret. Magic bytes '!RHY' (0x59485221) identify config location. Features AI-powered OCR for seed phrase extraction from images (v0.7+).

C++ infostealer often protected with VMProtect. Embeds legitimate DLLs (sqlite3.dll, mozglue.dll, freebl3.dll) in cleartext within the PE and dumps them to the working directory at runtime. Uses byte substitution tables shared with PrivateLoader plus XOR key 0x36 for message obfuscation. Communicates over custom TCP protocol on port 50500.

C-based infostealer with Python control panel. Uses polymorphic string obfuscation (unique ADD/SUB/XOR per sample), hash-based import resolution, and custom binary TCP protocol. Handshake identified by magic bytes 0x946F19B5 (LE B5 19 6F 94). C2 responds with 256-byte RC4 key for all subsequent communications. Targets 40+ browsers and 70+ crypto wallet extensions.

.NET infostealer with cross-platform support (Windows/Linux). Data serialized as XML via XmlSerializer, then gzip compressed, RC4 encrypted, and optionally RSA encrypted before exfiltration. Primary C2 via Tor network (.onion addresses) with secondary exfiltration via Telegram bot API. Known mutex 'kwnmsgyyay'. Features USB spreading capability.

C++ infostealer with Python control panel. Uses ChaCha20 encryption with Base64 encoding for payload and config file encryption. Connects to C2 early (before data collection, unlike most stealers). Exfiltrates Base64-encoded JSON over custom TCP protocol. Targets 95+ browser variants, 76 crypto wallet extensions, and 19 password managers including Windows Credential Manager/Vault.

.NET infostealer derived from RedLine Stealer codebase. Config stored in static .NET class with IP, ID, Message, and XOR Key fields. IP and ID fields are XOR-decrypted then double Base64-decoded. Uses WCF (Windows Communication Foundation) with NetTCPBinding over net.tcp:// protocol for C2. Obfuscated with Confuser Core 1.6.0.

macOS infostealer targeting Keychain passwords, browser data, and crypto wallets. Earlier versions written in Go, current in C++. Distributed as Mach-O universal binary (Intel x86_64 + Apple Silicon arm64). Uses multi-key XOR string encryption with tiered key selection based on string length. Prompts for credentials via AppleScript 'display dialog'. 2025 variant adds persistent backdoor with C2 polling loop.

Native C/C++ 64-bit DLL infostealer extremely focused on email credential theft (Outlook and Thunderbird). Compiled with Visual Studio 2008 with single export function named 'Entry'. Strings encrypted with cyclic XOR using key containing 'strela'. Uses volume serial ID as HTTP User-Agent for host fingerprinting. Geofenced to Germany, Spain, Italy, Ukraine. Associated with HIVE-0145 IAB.

.NET keylogger/stealer with triple exfiltration channels (SMTP, FTP, Telegram). Payload hidden in .RSRC section, AES-ECB encrypted. Recent variants delivered via AutoIt-compiled wrapper. Uses process hollowing into InstallUtil.exe via RunPE technique. Targets 50+ applications including browsers, email clients, and FTP clients.

C and x86 assembly infostealer/form grabber (FormBook pre-2020, XLoader post-2020 rebrand). Uses CRC32 Bzip2 variant for API hashing with lowercased function names. Custom RC4 implementation with 'positive unfold'. Generates decoy traffic to legitimate domains mixed with real C2 traffic. NOPUSHEBP encrypted functions contain dynamically constructed decryption keys. Heavy anti-analysis with virtualized code blocks.

Custom C++ loader used by initial access brokers since March 2022, linked to Conti/Quantum ransomware. Uses RC4-encrypted config in .data section with cleartext key alongside encrypted C2 list and campaign ID. Features APC injection (NtQueueApcThread) and reflective DLL loading via PowerSploit. User-agent string 'bumblebee' doubles as RC4 key for network encryption in early versions.

Highly evasive shellcode-based downloader using Vectored Exception Handler (VEH) for control flow obfuscation. Shellcode encrypted with multi-byte XOR key. Downloads payloads from cloud services (Google Drive, OneDrive). Uses modified DJB2 with XOR masking for API hashing (seed 5381). Anti-VM scans entire process memory for VM-related strings.

Modular bot and loader active since 2011. Stager injects main module into explorer.exe using process hollowing. Uses dual RC4 keys (4-byte DWORD each) for request/response encryption. Copies ntdll.dll to temp directory to bypass hooks. Version 2025 breaks compatibility with prior network protocols.

C++ proxy bot and backdoor widely used by ransomware operators (Ryuk, Conti, DarkSide, Black Basta) to set up SOCKS5 proxies for C2 traffic tunneling. Uses triple encryption for beacons (XOR -> RC4 -> XOR) with a 40-byte hardcoded key. For each infected host, C2 opens a new TCP port for SOCKS5 traffic.

C++ pay-per-install loader distributing up to 5000 infections per day. Uses SIMD PXOR instructions (XMM registers) for string decryption. Employs dead drop resolvers - 3 hardcoded URLs where first two return plaintext C2 address, third returns XOR-encrypted response. Shares byte substitution tables with RisePro stealer.

Loader believed to be the successor to IcedID, developed by Lunar Spider. First observed November 2023. Uses RC4 with 64-byte Base64-encoded key for C2 traffic encryption. String obfuscation (v1.4+) via AES-256-CTR with hardcoded key and per-string 16-byte IV. Campaign ID generated via FNV hash algorithm (e.g., 'Wiski' -> 0x24e7ce9e).

Loader and backdoor from the TrickBot group (Wizard Spider), active since April 2020. Uses Emercoin blockchain DNS (.bazar TLD) for C2 domain resolution via OpenNIC. C++ template metaprogramming generates per-build unique encryption routines, making static signatures extremely difficult. Process hollowing into svchost.exe for fileless execution.

Advanced modular backdoor in shellcode format used by Chinese APT groups (APT41, BRONZE ATLAS/UNIVERSITY) since 2017. Successor to PlugX. Network data compressed with QuickLZ then encrypted with generated AES key. Supports 6 C2 protocols (TCP, SSL, HTTP, HTTPS, UDP, DNS). Loaded via DLL sideloading into legitimate executables. Plugin-based architecture with modules loaded as shellcode.

RAT attributed to North Korean APT37 (Reaper/ScarCruft), active since 2014. Unique encryption approach where the AES decryption key is the Windows service name under which the malware runs. File exfiltration uses AES with IV from QueryPerformanceCounter and filename as key. Targets political organizations across Russia, East Asia, Europe, and Middle East.

Modular botnet and dropper written in C/C++, active since October 2018. Functions as infostealer and payload delivery platform. Sends system info via cleartext HTTP POST with distinctive parameter format. Drops credential stealer (cred64.dll) and clipper (clip64.dll) modules executed via rundll32.exe. Mutex via CreateMutexA exits if return value is 0xB7 (already exists).

Highly obfuscated worm attributed to Russian GRU unit 29155. Initially spreads via infected USB/LNK files, uses msiexec.exe to download payload from compromised QNAP NAS devices. Multi-layer packing with control flow flattening, Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) obfuscation, and opaque predicates. RC4 with 32-byte key for exploit storage. Tor-based C2 with 200+ domains. Anti-hook detection checks first byte of APIs against 0xB8 (hooked) vs 0x48 (original x64).

Highly modular C++ banking trojan and malware platform, successor to Dyre, active since September 2016. Operated by Wizard Spider (ITG23). Spawned BazarLoader and Anchor malware. Over 10 modules including web injects (injectDll), credential theft (pwgrab), SMB lateral movement (shareDll), EternalBlue exploitation (tabDll), and DNS-based C2 (anchor_dns). Some modules compiled in Delphi.

One of the oldest banking trojans, based on leaked ISFB source code (2010). Uses Serpent-CBC for C2 traffic encryption, RSA for key exchange, APLib for config compression, and CRC32 for API hashing. Config stored in encrypted .bss section with ADDON_MAGIC marker (e.g., 'JJ' / 0x4A4A) to locate config data. Dreambot variant adds DGA and Tor C2.

A Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) remote access trojan written in VB.NET first spotted by BlackFog in November 2025. Consolidates credential harvesting, data exfiltration, live surveillance, ransomware, DDoS, and bot-killing into a single browser-based dashboard. Automatically harvests browser-stored passwords, session cookies, and application tokens before operator interaction. Supports USB spreading, keylogging, crypto clipper, and UAC bypass.

First documented AI-powered ransomware proof-of-concept, discovered by ESET in August 2025. Written in Go, it queries a locally hosted LLM (via Ollama API using gpt-oss:20b model) to dynamically generate cross-platform Lua scripts at runtime for system enumeration, selective exfiltration, and SPECK-128 encryption. Destructive encryption function exists in code but remains inactive in early variants. Represents a paradigm shift where AI models orchestrate malware behavior.

File Collection via Lua Script Generation

description: Highly stealthy espionage backdoor discovered by Microsoft DART in November 2025. Abuses the legitimate OpenAI Assistants API as its sole C2 channel, disguising malicious traffic as normal AI API calls to evade network detection. Two-component architecture - obfuscated .NET loader (Netapi64.dll) and backdoor (OpenAIAgent.Netapi64). Uses AppDomainManager injection to persist within legitimate host processes such as developer tools. Obfuscated with Eazfuscator.NET.

Native C++ botnet loader discovered by Qrator Labs that decentralizes its C2 infrastructure using public smart contracts on the Polygon blockchain. Bots query public RPC endpoints to read encrypted commands from the blockchain ledger, making traditional domain/IP takedowns impossible. Operators deploy instructions via web dashboard to blockchain. Licensing at $200 for panel access or $4000 for full C++ source. Only ~$1 of MATIC enables 100-150 command transactions.

Destructive wiper attributed to Russia/Sandworm, first observed Feb 2022 targeting Ukrainian organizations. Abuses the legitimate EaseUS Partition Manager signed driver (empntdrv.sys) to gain raw disk access via DeviceIoControl, then corrupts MBR, NTFS ($MFT, $Bitmap), and FAT file systems on all enumerated physical drives (0-100).

Extremely compact (~9KB) destructive wiper attributed to Russia/Sandworm, discovered March 2022. Overwrites files with null bytes (first 0xA00000 bytes for files >10MB), then destroys partition tables on PhysicalDrive9 through PhysicalDrive0 by zeroing the first 1920 bytes. Avoids execution on domain controllers.

Go-based destructive wiper attributed to Sandworm (GRU Unit 74455), discovered January 2023. Deployed via Active Directory Group Policy. Deletes Volume Shadow Copies, then overwrites files in system directories and non-system drives with randomly generated 4096-byte blocks before forcing a system reboot.

Linux ELF wiper compiled for x86, an evolved variant of AcidRain (which targeted MIPS). Attributed to a Sandworm subcluster. Expands targeting to include UBI (flash memory), Device Mapper (LVM/RAID), MMC, SCSI/SATA, and MTD devices via IOCTL-based wiping. Overwrites targets with randomly generated 256KB buffers in multiple passes.

Cross-platform destructive wiper (PE and ELF variants) used by pro-Hamas hacktivist group targeting Israeli organizations since October 2023. Overwrites file contents with random data generated via Mersenne Twister PRNG, renames destroyed files with a random character sequence and appends the ".BiBi" extension. Purely destructive with no C2 communication or ransom demands. Uses aggressive multithreading (up to 12 threads).

Destructive wiper attributed to Sandworm with medium confidence, deployed against a Polish energy company on December 29, 2025. Three variants were deployed in rapid succession after iterative failures, each with slightly modified wiping code. Overwrites files using a single 16-byte random buffer generated at execution start. Built in a Vagrant environment using Visual Studio 2013.

Destructive wiper discovered by Cisco Talos in June 2025, targeting Ukrainian critical infrastructure. Deployed via a legitimate endpoint administration framework through a batch file. Creates one thread per drive/volume to overwrite NTFS filesystem artifacts ($MFT, $MFTMirr, $LogFile, $Boot, $Bitmap, $TxfLog, $Tops, $AttrDef) and MBR with randomly generated bytes.

Open-source Linux LKM rootkit supporting kernels 2.6.x through 6.x. Overwrites the syscall table to hook getdents/getdents64 (hide files/processes) and kill (signal-based control). Signal 63 toggles module visibility, signal 64 grants root. A 2024 variant masquerades as the x_tables Netfilter module with magic packet command execution.

Open-source Linux LKM rootkit that hooks filldir family functions rather than replacing entire syscalls, providing stealthier file/directory/process hiding. Features a port-knocking backdoor supporting TCP/UDP/ICMP magic packets. Used by UNC3886 (China-nexus) to maintain persistence on VMware ESXi guest virtual machines.

Sophisticated multi-stage Linux LKM rootkit discovered September 2024 by Elastic Security Labs. Architecture consists of a dropper ("cron"), two memory-resident executables, an LKM rootkit module (puma.ko), and a userland SO rootkit (Kitsune at lib64/libs.so). Uses ftrace to hook 18 syscalls and kernel functions. Targets pre-5.7 kernels.

Windows kernel-mode rootkit carrying a legitimate Microsoft WHQL digital signature. Targets online gamers in China. Redirects HTTP and HTTPS traffic through a custom proxy server drawn from a built-in list of approximately 300 randomly-generated domains on the .xyz TLD. Installs a custom root CA certificate for HTTPS interception.

Windows kernel-mode rootkit used by the GhostEmperor APT (China-nexus) targeting government entities and telecom companies in Southeast Asia. Bypasses Driver Signature Enforcement by abusing Cheat Engine's signed driver (dbk64.sys). Hooks nsiproxy.sys IOCTL dispatcher to conceal TCP connections. Updated 2024 variant adds EDR evasion via ProcessSignaturePolicy.

Windows kernel-mode rootkit used by the TunnelSnake APT (China-nexus) targeting diplomatic entities in Asia and Africa. Functions as a passive network implant using the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) to inspect incoming packets at the kernel level. Payload bytes are XORed with 0x05 then bit-negated. Bypasses DSE by abusing VirtualBox driver (VBoxDrv.sys v1.6.2).

Rust and Go-based Ransomware-as-a-Service with over 900 victims. Uses AES-256-CTR with AES-NI hardware acceleration (ChaCha20 fallback) and RSA-4096 for key protection. Supports credential harvesting via GPO and can encrypt via WSL ELF encryptors on Windows hosts.

Rust-based cross-platform ransomware emerged June 2024 with strong code overlap with BlackCat/ALPHV. Uses ChaCha20 for file encryption with RSA-protected symmetric keys. Supports Full, Fast, and Auto encryption modes with intermittent encryption for files >100MB. Targets Windows, Linux, ESXi, NAS, and PowerPC.

RaaS built on leaked Conti v3 source code, compiled with MinGW/GCC. Uses hybrid ChaCha20 + RSA encryption (AES-256 in older variants, ChaCha8 in newer). Employs BYOVD with rentdrv2_x64.sys and truesight.sys drivers to terminate AV/EDR via DeviceIoControl. Uses stack strings obfuscation.

Rust-based RaaS successor to Hive ransomware with approximately 60% code overlap. Uses AES encryption with hardware AES-NI instructions and RSA-OAEP for key wrapping with SHA3-256 Keccak hashing. Targets Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, and ESXi.

LockBit 3.0 builder derivative first observed August 2024. Windows variant uses Salsa20 + RSA-2048 encryption, lacks obfuscation and anti-debugging. Linux variant targets VMware ESXi servers. Exploits Zyxel firewall CVE-2024-42057 for initial access.

China-nexus C++ ransomware deployed via ShadowPad and PlugX backdoors in the Green Nailao campaign targeting European healthcare. First known ransomware to use SM2 elliptic curve cryptography for protecting AES-256-CTR file encryption keys. Delivered via DLL sideloading through usysdiag.exe loading sensapi.dll.

RaaS created by GhostSec hacktivist group, blurring hacktivism and cybercrime. Version 1.0 is Python-based compiled with Nuitka, using Fernet (AES-128-CBC) for file encryption. Version 2.0 rewritten in Golang for cross-platform support (Windows, Linux, VMware).

Cross-platform ransomware active since September 2024, targeting Windows (PE) and Linux/FreeBSD/ESXi (ELF). Uses AES-256-GCM for file encryption with RSA-4096 key wrapping. Deploys NodeSnake RAT (Node.js) and custom packed RAT for persistent access. Distributed via fake browser updates and ClickFix social engineering.

Most prevalent open-source cryptocurrency miner abused in malicious deployments. Supports RandomX (Monero), KawPow, CryptoNight, and GhostRider algorithms. Cross-platform PE/ELF binaries. Malicious variants typically modify donate.h to zero donation and embed hard-coded pool configuration.

Stealthy Linux cryptominer and backdoor active since at least 2021, targeting millions of Linux servers. Mimics legitimate system tools (perf + ctl naming). Deploys userland rootkit libgcwrap.so via LD_PRELOAD that hooks pam_authenticate and pcap_loop. Uses TOR for encrypted C2 and stops mining when users log in.

Premier Windows credential extraction tool by Benjamin Delpy. Extracts plaintext passwords, NTLM hashes, Kerberos tickets, and certificates from LSASS process memory. Used by 18+ ransomware groups and 43+ threat groups. Key modules include sekurlsa (credential dumping), lsadump (SAM/DCSync), and kerberos (ticket manipulation).

Open-source cross-platform credential recovery tool written in Python, often distributed as PyInstaller-compiled executables. Retrieves stored passwords from 60+ applications across browsers, email clients, databases, WiFi, sysadmin tools, and Git credentials. Used by 10+ threat groups including OilRig and MuddyWater.

Modular C++ backdoor used by APT41 (Brass Typhoon/Wicked Panda) since at least June 2021, with Windows PE and Linux ELF variants. Supports HTTP, TCP, KCP-over-UDP, and WebSocket (WSS) C2 channels. Configuration is XOR-encoded with a single-byte key (observed 0x59). Some variants use VMProtect packing.

Memory-resident modular backdoor framework attributed with medium confidence to the CoughingDown threat group. Deployed via ProxyLogon (CVE-2021-26855) exploitation against ISPs and government entities. Uses DLL hijacking of legitimate Windows services (MSDTC, IKEEXT, SessionEnv) to inject the backdoor. Plugin-based architecture with orchestrator DLL (internal name ssss.dll) exporting a single method "m".

Full-featured memory-resident macOS RAT attributed to the Lazarus Group (DPRK), targeting blockchain and cryptocurrency engineers via social engineering on Discord. Five-stage infection chain delivers Python scripts, SUGARLOADER (Mach-O dropper), and final KANDYKORN payload via reflective binary loading. Both SUGARLOADER and KANDYKORN use RC4 encryption with a hardcoded 64-byte key for C2 communications.

Complex HTTP(S) RAT attributed to the Lazarus Group, deployed via supply chain compromise. Named for distinctive "SIGNBT" prefixes in C2 traffic. Uses AES encryption with keys obtained during the SIGNBTLG handshake. Paired with LPEClient loader for victim profiling and payload delivery.

Long-running RAT attributed to the Lazarus Group, first discovered 2018 targeting Indian financial institutions. Dropper embeds encrypted payload as PE overlay, uses process hollowing to inject into system processes. Multi-layer encryption using modified RC4, RC5, and RC6 algorithms varies per sample.

Fourth major iteration of the Turla (Snake) APT group's signature backdoor, in development since 2007. Defining feature is using Gmail web interface for C2 via cookie-based authentication. Uses a virtual FAT16 file system encrypted with AES-256 in XTS mode to store configuration, logs, and operational files.

Custom x64 C-language backdoor deployed by MuddyWater (Iranian MOIS) since May 2024, replacing previously favored RMM tools. Configuration strings and C2 communications obfuscated by subtracting a hardcoded byte value (commonly 3) from each byte. Communicates over raw TCP on port 443. Targets Middle East and European organizations.

Custom fileless and socketless 64-bit Windows backdoor attributed to Volt Typhoon, active since at least July 2019 targeting U.S. defense contractors and critical infrastructure. Hijacks legitimate process network sockets using the Microsoft Detours library to hook the Winsock accept() function. Converted to shellcode using the Donut framework and injected via PowerSploit.

Rust-based post-exploitation tool discovered by Unit 42 in September 2024. Uses JSON-formatted ImplantConfig with embedded C2 credentials and HTTPS-encrypted task synchronization. Typical samples are ~7MB due to Rust runtime.

Open-source Go-based C2 remote control platform that establishes reverse SSH tunnels for fully interactive shells. Deployed via Docker with a web management UI supporting team collaboration, multi-platform client payloads, and crypto-mining operations. Over 1000 active C2 IPs tracked from January 2024.

Open-source cross-platform RAT written in Go, first published March 2022. Uses WebSocket C2 communication over port 8000 with a web-based management UI. Used in DragonSpark campaign where threat actors employed Golang source code interpretation to evade static analysis.

Golang-based reimplementation of the QUASAR RAT discovered by Elastic Security Labs, deployed via the SADBRIDGE loader packaged as MSI using Advanced Installer. Features AMSI/ETW patching, DLL side-loading via x64dbg.exe/x64bridge.dll, and retains protocol compatibility with original QUASAR server on default port 1080.

In-memory .NET RAT discovered by Morphisec in March 2025, targeting healthcare and pharmaceutical organizations. Uses .NET resource resolver hijacking to execute entirely in RAM, AES-256-CBC encrypted payloads compressed with GZip, and ProtoBuf-serialized C2 communication. Delivered via DLL side-loading through hpreader.exe.

Rust-based cross-platform P2P worm targeting Redis deployments via CVE-2022-0543 (Lua sandbox escape) and Redis SLAVEOF replication. Deploys XMRig miner, ransomware, and a dynamically-generated usermode rootkit. Uses UPX packing and communicates over a custom P2P protocol on ports 60100-60150.

Mirai-based Linux botnet discovered by Akamai in January 2023, compiled with uClibc instead of GCC to evade Mirai detection signatures. Spreads via SSH brute-force with a distinctive "hi" probe message, deploys a modified XMRig miner with encrypted configuration and custom mining pool.

JavaScript-based loader/downloader active since 2017, operated by Mustard Tempest with ties to Evil Corp. Uses drive-by downloads via compromised websites presenting fake browser update lures. Delivers Cobalt Strike, NetSupport RAT, RansomHub ransomware, and other payloads. Dominated ~40% of loader detections in early 2025.

Modular banking trojan/loader derived from leaked Zeus source code, resurrected in 2019 as "Silent Night". Updated in September 2023 with RSA-encrypted C2, DGA, DNS tunneling, and native 64-bit support. Uses Zeus BinStorage format with 1024-bit RSA + RC4 + Zeus VisualEncrypt layered encryption.

Modular backdoor attributed to APT41/Winnti Group, active since at least 2010 with both PE and ELF variants. Core component handles C2 communication and plugin deployment. Uses AES-CTR encryption with libtomcrypt library and counter value derived from string "q@3$%hy*&u". Linux variant abuses LD_PRELOAD with Azazel-based userland rootkit for persistence.

Chinese-origin RAT attributed to the Silver Fox threat group. Uses custom reversed UTF-16LE config encoding with pipe-delimited fields and pinyin key abbreviations. Communicates over raw TCP/UDP on non-standard ports. Typically delivered via DLL sideloading through tracerpt.exe. Known for process hollowing injection, security tool disabling, and registry persistence.
